argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean certification claim: the admissible record supports certifying for launch on aggregate readiness grounds only if the audit packet and model card are corrected to disclose the unresolved enterprise password recovery limitation. The aggregate readiness pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch-readiness, but the unresolved slice weakness, the draft state of the mitigation runbook, and the stated policy do not support a no-limitations certification narrative. On that record, the appropriate treatment is caveated compliance rather than suspicion of an unsupported clean approval.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency claim is needed. The business-relevant point from the admissible record is that escalation over a clean-certification theory is avoidable if the auditor distinguishes between prohibited clean certification and supportable certification with an explicit disclosed limitation. Treating those as the same outcome would overstate the compliance gap.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling point. It says certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that standard is met, because the mitigation artifact is still draft and has TBD fields. But the same policy text does not say launch certification is forbidden in all other cases; it says current disclosure is still required unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. That makes a disclosed-limitation certification packet policy-consistent, while a clean no-limitations packet would not be.
concessions: The current record does not support certification without material caveats.
The draft mitigation runbook is not sufficient to remove the disclosure requirement because owner and alert threshold remain unspecified.
Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring norms, but it does not by itself prove internal policy compliance.
The auditor is correct that aggregate readiness and rehearsal summaries do not eliminate the need to review the final packet language for the required limitation disclosure.
